Testimony on LD 1724 the Baxter State Park Authority to Convey Certain Land in Cumberland County
May 6, 2025
Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry: my name is Aaron Megquier, and I serve as Executive
Director of Friends of Baxter State Park.
Friends of Baxter State Park strongly supports LD 1724. This resolve would authorize - but not
compel-the Baxter State Park Authority to convey the Austin Cary Lot in Harpswell to a new
owner. Legislative approvalfor this conveyance is required by the Maine Designated Lands Act.
The Austin Cary Lot was originally acquired by the Maine Forest Authority in 1973 and 1974 using
funds from a trust established by Percival Baxter for land acquisition. When the Maine Forest
Authority was abolished in 1984, ownership of the Austin Cary Lot passed first to the Bureau of Parks and Lands, and then to the Baxter State Park Authority. Deed restrictions on the property require that the Austin Cary Lot be used for a demonstration forest, wildlife management area, or
other educational and scientific uses for 99 years from the dates of the original conveyances in 1973 and 1974. If conveyed, the Baxter State Park Authority will ensure via deed restrictions that
the new owner will uphold management in accordance with Governor Baxter's trust as well as the
existing deed restrictions.
Management of the Austin Cary Lot has posed a significant challenge for Baxter State Park staff for over 40 years. The Austin Cary Lot is more than 220 miles by road from the Scientific Forest Management Area in Baxter State Park. This is comparable to the drive from Augusta, Maine to Providence, Rhode Island. Baxter State Park has no staff based in Cumberland County, or anywhere in southern Maine. Due to these logistical challenges, the Park has relied on the services of a contracted forester for many years - an option that has worked well for managing the land and would also be available to any landowner. The time and resources devoted to the Austin Cary Lot could be better spent on the many management challenges facing Baxter State Park.
This transfer would have significant benefits for the local community. A different owner with nearby staff and a more locally focused mission will likely be able to work more effectively with
neighboring landowners and be more responsive to the needs of local communities.
Friends of Baxter State Park fully supports the Park's position on this issue. We believe that LD 1724 is in the best interests of Baxter State Park, the Harpswell community, and the Maine public. We
urge the Committee on Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry to vote ought to pass on this bill.

Testimony in Support of HP 151 / LD 1724 Resolve, Authorizing the Baxter State Park Authority to Convey Certain Land in Cumberland County Submitted by James O'Malley Licensed Forester and SFMA Advisory Committee Member Fort Kent, Maine April 25, 2025
Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker and Honorable Members of the Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry Committee:
My name is Jame O'Malley, and I am a licensed forester living in Fort Kent, Maine. I have had the honor of serving on the Scientific Forest Management Area (SFMA) Advisory Committee for Baxter State Park since 2010. I am writing today in support of HP 151 / LD 1724, which authorizes the Baxter State Park Authority to convey a small parcel of land in Cumberland County.
This parcel lies far outside the boundaries of Baxter State Park and has no functional or ecological connection to the Park or the SFMA. As such, it falls outside the scope of the Park's mission, which is focused on preserving the wilderness character and natural resources of the land generously gifted by Governor Baxter.
In my advisory work with the SFMA, I've seen firsthand the importance of aligning land stewardship with mission-driven goals. Retaining ownership of a non-contiguous, unrelated parcel creates administrative challenges and distracts from the Park Authority's core responsibilities. Allowing this conveyance would support better land management outcomes-- both for the Park and for the community better positioned to manage and benefit from this parcel.
I believe this resolve is a responsible and practical solution. It honors the intent of Governor Baxter's vision while recognizing the value of local land management and stewardship. I urge you to vote "Ought to Pass" on HP 151 / LD 1724.
Thank you for your time and for your dedication to Maine's public lands.
Respectfully,
James O'Malley Licensed Forester 1014 Member, SFMA Advisory Committee since 2010

Testimony of Nava Tabak, Natural Resource Director Baxter State Park
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry Public Hearing Date: May 6, 2025
In support of LD 1724: "Resolve Authorizing the Baxter State Park Authority to Convey Certain Land in Cumberland County"
Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry, my name is Nava Tabak, I am the Natural Resource Director for Baxter State Park. I am testifying in support of LD 1724, A Resolve Authorizing the Baxter State Park Authority to Convey the Austin Cary Lot, an undeveloped state-owned property in the Town of Harpswell, Cumberland County.
Encompassing over 200,000 acres in northern Maine, Baxter State Park is the state's largest protected area. The Park is a unique public charitable trust that is administered by the Baxter State Park Authority and is financially independent; it draws no General Fund dollars from the state. The Park includes the Scientific Forest Management Area - a nearly 30,000-acre area that is managed to demonstrate sustainable and scientific forestry.
Many people are surprised to learn that the Baxter State Park Authority also manages the Austin Cary Lot, a 228-acre property located over 200 miles away from Baxter State Park on Sebascodegan Island in Harpswell (Figure 1). The Austin Cary Lot was originally managed by the Maine Forest Authority (1973-1983), and then by the Bureau of Public Lands (1983-1985), before being transferred to the Baxter State Park Authority in 1985. This transfer to the Baxter State Park Authority was the result of common threads between Baxter State Park's Scientific Forest Management Area and the Austin Cary Lot: both are managed primarily for sustainable forestry pursuant to deed restrictions.
Unlike the Scientific Forest Management Area in the north Maine woods, the Austin Cary Lot is dominated by a forest typical of mid-coast Maine and is bisected by the tidal water and wetlands of Long Marsh (Figure 2). It is neighbored by similarly forested coastal areas, residences, a business, and the Harpswell Community School. Both the Austin Cary Lot's geographic distance from the Park and the significant differences in the conditions of the Scientific Forest Management Area and the Austin Cary Lot (including their ecology, land use

history, operational logistics, and public uses of the respective properties), have continually presented management challenges for Baxter State Park. Baxter State Park has long recognized that another entity may be better positioned to manage the Austin Cary Lot.
Like many lands managed by the Bureau of Parks and Lands, the Austin Cary Lot is subject to Article IX, Section 23 of Maine's Constitution, which requires 2/3 legislative approval to convey the Austin Cary Lot, and to the Designated Lands Act. Passage of LD 1724 would allow--but not require--the Baxter State Park Authority to transfer ownership of the Austin Cary Lot to an interested party. The conveyance would be subject to deed restrictions that will require that the Austin Cary Lot continue to be used primarily for sustainable forestry or wildlife management, while allowing for compatible educational, scientific, and recreational uses. These are the purposes envisioned for the property by former Governor Baxter1 and the property's former owners, who aimed to serve the interest of the people of Maine in conserving the property. The Park supports the proposed amendment to LD 1724, which clarifies that such a transaction would be in the purview of Baxter State Park, a state agency independent from the Bureau of Parks and Lands.
Transferring ownership of the Austin Cary Lot represents an opportunity to provide this unique property with the tailored and consistent management it requires. The interest of the people of Maine, as manifested in publicly beneficial uses of the property, would be protected by the deed restrictions required by LD 1724. It could be further enhanced by additional land conservation in Cumberland County resulting from the proceeds of a sale, and the Park also supports the proposed amendment to LD 1724, which specifies that such proceeds would be committed to the Public Reserved Lands Acquisition Fund of the Bureau of Parks and Lands for this purpose. (Pursuant to Article IX, Section 23 of the Maine Constitution and the Designated Lands Act, any proceeds received from the sale of the Austin Cary Lot must be used to acquire real estate in the same county for the same purposes.) The Harpswell community also stands to benefit from more effective collaborative opportunities under new management of the Austin Cary Lot.
Please vote LD 1724 out of committee as ought to pass. And thank you for the opportunity to testify.

Should public use of this land increase in the future, then the property owner needs to take a much larger role
in the maintenance of the road, as discussed in the last section of my testimony.

4. Need tor afliarify Share of Read Maintenance iosts
BSP has indicated to our Road Association that they don't need to maintain a quality access road since their only need has been to access timber harvests with heavy equipment. But even though BSP's representative

has voted against the Association's annual budgets at times, BSP has paid a share of the expenses, and I believe that has most recently been one-seventh of the cost of the road maintenance. But the two deeds to the property, referenced above, have a predecessor deed (Book 2830 Page 242) and this deed references an agreement in Book 2604 Page 91 that clearly states that one-third of the cost of maintaining the majority of the road was to be borne by the Haws, and the other two-thirds was to be borne by the two other property owners. The land owned by the Haws was the land that eventually became the Austin Cary Lot, so I believe that the future owner of the Austin Cary Lot should be responsible for a third of
the cost of this road, and that should be included in any legi�lative transfer of thisiproperty. I am happy to
provide copies of these deeds and the connection between them for the work session.
To reiterate, while I understand that the Baxter State Park Authority would like to find a new steward of this special piece of land in order to focus more on their core mission at Baxter State Park, l believe that this particular piece of legislation is premature. The legislature needs to determine the specific new owner of the
Austin Cary Lot and to put in appropriate safeguards and requirements, including those that I've listed here
today.
Thank you for the opportunity to present these concerns to you today, and I'm happy to answer any questions
that you may have.
